From Fiameta April 1, 1998
Editoria.
It calls for a Belief from the Bottom of the Hear.
It has been five years since the existence of the legislation of the free press has become legally approved.
Although a lot could be said about the fact that proclamation 34/85 is not clear and from the angle of the penalty it may bring about on the free press it has its own share of making sure that the foundation and central pillar of democracy, the right to speak and write, and prohibition of censor ship has been legalized.
Side by side the products of the free press even before the press proclamation was decreed, and after, that, are paying heavy sacrifice with regards to the people's right to know, and has contributed one big chapter in the history of our country.
The freedom to speak and write has, once again, been validated. .
For the first time in the history of the country, numerous newspapers and magazines grew and developed people's out look.
The existence of newspapers and magazines by itself is not an end.
What's called press freedom is not the bodily existence of the press products.
Products of the press should publish and disclose all the news that need to reach the public so that the government could work openly and in a legal way.
Performing the work of the free press means, with out government intervention, the journalist delivering news to the public in a responsible feeling and assisting to amend themselves by criticizing the destructive tendencies of the government..
Is the Ethiopian Free Press in a level that could do this?.
No.
The reason it could not do this emanates from the free press itself and especially from EPRDF, gov't from which it claimed "the freedom was gotten by my struggle".
There could be shortage of experience on the side of the free press.
As a result, it can not be said there aren't any problems out of the ethics of journalism.
This straightforward flaw, however, the free press is the mouthpiece of oppositions."
The free press is the gathering of the defeated sides.
Having claimed that there was no need to attack with the sword of propaganda.
Before teaching and correcting, there's no problem that could be resolved by chasing and arresting the free press journalists.
Basically there is no reason a journalist could be arrested claiming for investigation due to press crime, unless he/she is sentenced to imprisonment.
When we analyze the problems of the free press today in our country, we don't see the government in power has a belief from the bottom of the heart from the widening of democracy and strengthening of the free press in our country.
The products of the free press that are seen in Addis Ababa and few towns of the country, if they were intended to show off the democracy, a great intrigue is being made on the democracy.
The people want the government of the people, a government which hears the queries of the people, and a government that works openly and legally.
And to bring about such a government, the people do not have a better tool other than expressing its ideas feely, willingly voting.
For this, the principal forum is the free press.
Those who open a hate-campaign on the free press are the only ones who went to live on the shoulders of the people without the willingness of the people.
It's not without a reason that we say that there's no interest among the current governors to strengthen the free press.        .
On the one hand, the incumbent party and the government structure it controls strengths its own propaganda Medias, it opens a propaganda campaign on the free press which operate on small financial and human resource capability.
From the perspective of the press law and the country's other legislations, while journalists, who committed press crime could be accused and, if found guilty, penalized, they are gathered and put behind bars by investigation departments.                                    .
The Campaign opened by the EPRDF's press "Revolutionary Democracy" recently and the campaign opened against Ethiop, Wenchif, Urji and other newspapers openly shows the not-so-good attitude the government has on the free press.
The sanction befell up on newspapers and magazines not to promote their papers in radio and television, the now-and-then penalty of imprisonment and money upon the editors of free press are not the reflections of good attitude.
According to the very many letters we receive form the public, reading a free press for a government worker may lead him/her to be considered as opposition and even lead to be evaluated.
Especially in the Tigray and Amhara regions the products of the press are read in secret.
It means that the people are made to be out of the democratic process.
The press law itself which has counted five years since its inception should be viewed again from the perspective of constitutional decree.
The EFDR constitution, Article 29 the rights to have a different out look and to express one's ideas freely "could be sanctioned only based on the laws that would be decreed on the principle that the freedom to get access of ideas and information could not be sanctioned by its content of ideas and the result of ideas it may bring about," it has such a forceful expression.
The press law was not amended in line with this principle..
Charges are still filed against newspapers claiming "troubling people's ideas".
The constitution knows the right to get information.
But the free press is forbidden to get government's information.
If the free press is strengthened the beneficiary is not only the public.
Press for the government is a principal method of looking in to itself and take measures of correction.
And a government which doesn't look into itself would eventually lead itself to failure. .
Therefore, government would be the first beneficiary if it evaluates its outlook on the free press and make corrections, at the 5th anniversary of the press proclamation.
Confrontation with the free press and democratic forces wouldn't take anywhere.
Hence, the problems we pointed out at this juncture should be viewed properly.
It is only then that we can say that democracy and free press are believed from the bottom of the heart by the current power holders..
From Tobia October 23, 1997
Message from Fiameta
The Key to control the currently spreading malaria epidemic is to establish its own organization.
Since recently even the highland areas of Ethiopia have been hearts of mosquito and it's not only regrettable to see many people dying but also make historically accountable in the future.
The fact that there was an independent center for malaria-control on a national level with different branches elsewhere that was established based on a research that epidemic would occur in certain temperate Zones and lowland areas, spraying pesticides including with airplane, teaching both victims of malaria and those who aren't infected with it used to play an important role, and as a result, malaria has never been major enemy to Ethiopian people..
As soon as the EPRDF government took power it demolished this office and, in the pretext of restructuring, assigned it to be established in the regional administration giving ay to the scattering of professionals, and the problem was created..
If quick measures are not taken with clear understanding to avert the situation, the number of casualties will escalate. .
Although the people In Gojam, Northern and Eastern Shoa have long become victims of malaria, it won't be a panacea to accuse one another, rather than seeking immediate solution..
To oust the minister of Health from his position or taking measures on others couldn't be a solution..
Malaria epidemic just like locust plague is a campaign that is to be launched nation-wide and continent-wise in combination, not something to be left only for the regions..
So, we recommend that a nation wide malaria control and prevention office be established, and let the urgent task of protection and wiping away of malaria starts.     .
From Fiameta February 19, 1999
Ethiopia Accepted the Lifting of the sanction on Ammunition
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed that Ethiopia accepted the decision to lift the sanction from getting access to ammunition the day before yesterday which the United Nations had put on Ethiopia and Eritrea..
In a statement the ministry of foreign affairs released yesterday, it said that the fact that the Security Council expressed the sanction from getting access of ammunition which had been put on both countries wouldn't continue pointed out that the sanction is lifted..
The sanction from accessing ammunition the Security Council had put on for the last year reminded Ethiopia that injustice act of being sufferer of aggression, she was equally became victim of the sanction like the aggressor, the statement disclosed.
The statement that was released form the Security Council the day before yesterday reminded that in order to bring about stability in the horn of Africa, both countries should focus on economic development and negotiation rather than buying ammunition and other military activities, yet, Ethiopia, from the very beginning, when aggression was waged against her, believed that the international community would condemn the aggression, and this would happen.    .
The peaceful effort Ethiopia has been making to reverse the situation, not able to call her aggressor an aggressor and the fact that she couldn't execute international law, her effort became futile, the statement disclosed.
However, the lesson that was gotten form the past experience an aggressor should not, in any way, be encouraged, and it is only then that countries who gave precedence for their economic development would, without any impediment, meet their goals, the statement disclosed..
The statement disclosed that it is only then that lasing peace and stability would reign in the continent..
From Addis Zemen May 17, 2001 .
Ethiopia and Eritrean currency are said to be changed on the same date!!
While it has been several months since Eritrean made it official that Ethiopian Birr can be exchanged for "Nakfa", she hasn't made it operational yet.
The associate reports for Fiameta in Asmara quoting some sources said that both currencies would be changed on the same date.
The Eritrean currency has not been changed because Ethiopia hasn't been showing any interest on the issue, said the report quoting Teka Beyene, Eritrean Bank Governor.
But according to the recent agreement it is reported that both parties would change the previous Birr.
Although Eritrea proposed for both currencies to have equal exchange value, Ethiopia proposed that they should conduct commercial transactions with (American) dollar when they deal with big business.
This idea of putting dollar more often than Nakfa in trade troubles Eritrean officials..
The idea that the potential value of Nakfa could become lower as compared to Ethiopian Birr has been held by many people from various quarters.
Eritrean Bank governor Ato Taka Beyene, on his part, said that Eritrean Nakfa would be evaluated at the end of every fiscal year would be discussed upon and measures would be taken.
There are some observers who claim that this means if Nakfa's exchange values deteriorate, Eritreans would have once again a dream of using Ethiopian Birr..
In connection of this it was reported that the future Ethio-Eritrean trade relations would put Nakfa's buying power into question, for Ethiopia doesn't have many items to import from Eritrea.
On the other hand, Nakfa's impact on Ethiopian Birr is very negligible and its power many even be less than the present currencies in Somalia and Djibouti..
Meanwhile, both parties had been conducting continous meetings so as to make the change of the previous currency operational the same day.
Internal sources also suggest that the change may be take place in one of the Saturdays..

From Fiameta September 15, 1999
Sudan Disclosed it is only Sudan and Egypt that have Priority Right on the Use of Abay River..
Sherif Al Tuhami, Sudanese Minister of Irrigation and Water Resources in the statement he gave to Reuters on Monday, said since Sudan and Egypt have for 700 years based their civilizations and agriculture on Abay, they have priority rights with regards to the use of Abay..
The minister who discussed about this issue last Monday with Reuters, stated that his country planned to build hydroelectric dams using Abay water, and for the construction they invited private foreign companies and the begotten product is said to be sold, he pointed out.
For the question Reuter asked him about Ethiopia's interest regarding the equitable share of Abay Rivers, he replied Ethiopia has to put forward he request for discussion and if it's not against the utilization procedure, he said, they'll find ways to cooperate with her..
And by saying so tried to present Ethiopia as if she doesn't have rights..
Asked what if Ethiopia wanted to use more water and took her own measure, Tuhami replied that I don't think Ethiopia would do that..
They know what this may result in..
It's very dangerous, he said..
Ethiopia which is the source of Tikur abay river doesn't know about the agreement Egypt and Sudan made pertaining to the division of water in 1959.
This agreement allocated 55.8 billion cubic meter water to Egypt while Sudan would take 18.5 billion cubic meter water..

From Fiameta December 30, 1999
A Daily Newspaper which is to be Distributed in Six Countries would start Publication on Monday
The company named "sub-saharan Informer" has completed its preparation to publish a colored daily newspaper that is to make its appearance in six African countries, including Ethiopia..
The English newspaper whose name is said to be "The Sub-Informer" would have 32 pages and is decided to make its distribution 124 thousand copies each day, the company disclosed. .
Sub-sharan Informer which has opened bureau for months in different African countries and have been studying the market, has how laid all the necessary preparations for publications..
According to the information gathered from the organization the publication of the news paper begins in Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Nairobi, Tanzania and Uganda..
The largest number of copies of the newspaper, 37 thousand, would be distributed in Nigeria while the lowest number of publication is 5 thousand which is in Ethiopia..
The content of the newspaper is divided into two: The part where common news is shared among all the countries, and special features prepared especially for each country's consumption would be the other part.
It's disclosed that the company's offices opened in different countries would combine and organize their news through the internet..
When the newspaper publication starts in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia after 8 months, the number of countries where the newspaper would be available rises to nine, and daily distribution of the paper would also rise to double 240 thousand, the company stated its plans.  .
With at least 8 of its pages being colored, the Sub-Saharn Informer would be the first news paper to be available in many African countries..
The cost of advertisement publication the company asks for would be fair and the market price of a newspaper is 3 Birr and 50 cents, the company disclosed.   .
From Addis Admas January 12, 200.
The American Government Signed A 30 Million Birr Agreemen.
Makele:- The American government signed a 30 million Birr agreement yesterday with Tigray National Regional Government and non-government organizations, which operate in the region..
The offered money would be expended on residence houses of Gule Mehada and Irob Districts ruined by the war, health institutions, schools, water projects and to protect the explosives, to give strengthened education on HIV AIDS and for the purchasing of goods, the regional administration disclosed.  .
The aid agreement was signed by American Ambassador to Ethiopia Mr. Tibor Nadze and Tigrean Region Regional Administrative Government social Department Head Dr Solomon Enquay and representatives of Tigray Development Association, the Catholic Aid Service, Cooperation International and Medicine San Frontiers..
Out of the offered money, 16 million Birr would be expended through Tigrean Development Association..
In his speech during this time, Ambassador Tibor Nadze pointed out that the American government has strong relationship with Tigrean people and reminded that earlier his government distributed 167 thousand tons of cereals of foods for those who were displaced from their house and proportions by war and victims of drought, and is now giving aid for execution of development works..
Dr. Solomon Enquacy on his part pointed out that the regional government and non-governmental organizations have been prepared to work together and thanked the American government for the aid it offered.
The displaced people from Gulo Mehada and Irob District people who were present during the aid agreement suggested that even though their invaded homes were freed by the heroic army, the magnitude of looting conducted was so high and the area was enclosed by explosives, they're still living in the bushes and fields, so called for other governments to follow suit..

From Fiameta June 3, 1998
The 50th Anniversary of Addis Ababa Chamber of Commerce was Celebrated with different occasions
The 50th anniversary of the Addis Ababa Chamber of Commerce is being celebrated from November 4, 1998 up to November 14, 1998 with international trade fair symposium and different festivities.
In the 3rd Addis Chamber International Trade Fair which was intended to coincide with the occasion, 181 organizations, local and foreign, predicated and presented their produces, out of which 64 of them were foreign companies.
This trade fair which was believed to play a pivotal role in widening trade and investment, connecting seller and buyer as well as strengthening technological transition, would be open for 12 days from November 4, 1998 onwards.
In relation to this trade fair, an international symposium under the leading aim "making the most of Ethiopian Economic Environment" was held from November 9-10, 1998.
In this symposium that was held in African Economic Commission meeting hall, higher government officials, local and foreign elites and business delegates presented research papers that pointed out the problems and remedies of Ethiopian local and international trade..
Among the papers presented, in order to benefit from international trade and investment, Ethiopia needs political and social stability and it is expected from the government to play a crucial role in strengthening and encouraging the private sector.

From Addis Zemen June 20, 2001 .
Editorial
Where is the Direction?
EPRDF's press "Abiyotawi Democracy" last week categorized, including Tobia, the free press "gathering of the Defeated and that operate on the support by opposition sides".
In no time more than 10 editors and publishers of newspapers were arrested.
Three weekly newspapers, that is, Ethiop, wenchif and Urji became out of publication.
The solution shouldn't have been additional assault.
Point in at someone saying that he/she works in the free press wouldn't bring about any good.
"who are you?"
a question would follow.
Instead, what's of worth is giving focus on the information and suggestions the free press offered and corrects one's mistakes on time.
Although we took the suggestion as mere gossip of enemies of democracy that can not support itself with tangible evidence, we would still like to make clear one major issue about the publications of Tobia and its publisher, Akpak.
As a member of free press, when Akpak rose to give service to make public, it was confident of the wide and rich experience of its members, as well as truth and quality of the mind.
From the outset, it doesn't hold any grudges against another. .
Based on what the Ethiopian law commands it was establish had by a capital of 15 people, but it is not the property of one or two people.
When Akpak was established as a publisher of press it took as a light of leading principle not forgetting the responsibility it had for the public, not including favoring political organizations in its work, rather focus on public awareness.
As those sides who do not wish the strengthening of democracy and free press claim, there is no part of the public or party the publication of Akpak favors.
They are forums of free ideas.
It would perform its tasks today and in the future sticking to this principle.
Indeed since it holds the ideas of wide country rather than narrow area, unity rather than difference, love rather than hat red and grudges and since it doesn't accept racial politics, the beneficiaries of the present wind may not like it.
If through the conspiracy anti-press and anti-democratic forces it encounters peril, we won't have tears to shed for there are many young Ethiopians who have made their positions clear to make democracy reign, to serve the mistreated people.
Ethiopia usually gives birth after birth to children who would sacrifice for her.
And the fact that she delivers is being openly witnessed.
Among those who suffer from this regime, became victims of attack and professionals, who frequent hardship, the army of the press is the first and the main one.
Free press is the central pillar and mainstay of democracy.
Free press means the enemy of dictatorial regime.
It means exposing and struggling the injustice and power corruptors.
Therefore, the more the free press members are imprisoned and suffered, the better they feel about their performance that they display with great sacrifice.
They feel proud, not ashamed about it.
When ever dictators tossed and turned, the press they established for the purpose of fanning perfidy and releasing poisonous propaganda cried over nothing, it seems to us that the many journalists who are imprisoned would be consoled.
It is known that we are found in a regime where the prisoners are mostly prisoners of conscience, leaders of political organizations and members, as well as journalists who are conscience of the public.
This situation hasn't changed or improved from day to day.
Had it improved, it would have given the regime a better look.
Nonetheless, the current government is exposed be fore the world in its human rights violation, lack of democratic characteristics, and in its suppression of free press.
The present Prime Minister Mr. Meles Zenawi, who was mentioned by name as one of the ten enemies of the free press, doesn't make anyone proud.
It's not patriotism.
We found condemnation, not admiration in history for a leader who brought suffering to his own fellow people.
The number of journalists who became victims of police and central investigation and were put to the routine threatening prison cells as of recent weeks are many.
Journalists whom the court hasn't passed verdict and whose life are in the police stations and prisons are getting numerous.
Although the young writers who previously were imprisoned for a year and above and were released have borne the pain, it would be difficult to expect to share the pain an innocent citizen undergoes in prison in vain.
It is an experience to show that the democracy and justice which was said to live in our country is now being ejected.
As if the drama which was played in the pretext to law was not sufficient, the newspaper of the ruling party, government, so-called press of organizations attempted to spread malicious gossips and back biting calling the free press and journalists by name.
This doesn't allow the fifth row press that "suppresses" the benefit, security and unity of the people to have legality as well as publicity.
We know what these groups who say "We are journalists; we are the ones who present the right news; we are discharging the duties of the press" are practically performing.
The Ethiopian people, too, know it well.
However we don't think the hired ones know themselves.
We don't miss the fact that the malicious gossip they spread mentioning legal organizations and journalists by name has been the mission and duty they were given from their bosses.    .
Their direction is towards destroying the free press through propaganda as well as using force, so fellow people who say that they stand for the people and democracy, should know it in advance.
It is impossible to think of democracy without free press.
It's not possible to prove being a democrat suppressing and weakening the free press.

As a result, the economic development strategy of EPRDF makes the regions and farmers central where all development forces participate and the majority of the people. At each level becomes beneficiary and where speedy progress would be registered, the spokesperson pointed out..
To this end, the crucial role is that of the people and the investor while the government focuses on establishing infrastructures, arranging the control and follow-up and building the implementation capacity of the leadership who are engaged in development activities of regions, zones and districts, it was pointed out..
The comparative economic freedom would be assured in this economic path an EPRDF's development path being capitalist, it made the Ethiopian farmer who constitutes 85 percent and the regions central, the spokesperson disclosed. .
And this would enable the wide participation of capitalists of the country, develop government's role and would give special focus on backward areas, which has comparative freedom..
However, the mixed outlook held by members was not made to be amended, so there was a situation where the previous outlook was seen in daily lives, and important discussion was underway with regards to the outlook issue, it disclosed.  .

A Holy Father by the name Aba Ketsela Mengistu who has been serving in Ethiopian Orthodox Church at different parishes in Gospel services, and who was called heretic by a tabloid which is named "Sematsedk" condemned it by saying that calling me "heretic" is just a devil's talk..
It is known that hatred that sustained between the two sides of the Orthodox Church has been aggravating, clouds of concern hung in the minds of many church people that this might shake the unified pillar of the Church.
Aba Ketsela who sent the details of accusations charged against many children of the church, not excluding himself, quoting sematsedk newspaper, condemned it, is now living in North America, Canada as Head of Preaching Gospel Department with the Ethiopian Orthodox Church..
I was saddened by what was written about me as heretic in 1998.
I served the church by my skills that are teaching presentation, song, poetry, sacrificial songs..
After I became a monk, I reached from priesthood to elder priest and I never declined form serving the Orthodox Church..
And at the moment in North America (Canada) where I live, I am the Son of the Orthodox church who indulged in preaching gospel and I'm not heretic, and I want to disclose that the disseminated news against me is fruitless, he said..
The news which reached us crossing different continents broadly details Aba Ketsela's grievance against his being called heretic, who said Bishop Merha Kirstos and Bishop Nathnael are my all-time witnesses who taught me the secret of Flesh, the content of the Bible and its interpretations..
"Aba" who has served in preaching the gospel in Miskaye Hazunan Medhanealm monastery and other parishes in Addis Ababa for so many years, and when moved to Canada he was really sad for hearing about his being called heretic and put forward a message reminding the Christian congregation not to be misled by the gossip around.
There are some who claimed that this false allegation of being heretic on many people including Aba Ketsela in not only the problems of the individuals but it is the problem that gradually came to the Orthodox Church..
Most of the people charged in the aforesaid tabloid, were not only suspended from work and salary, but also places like Debre Libanos Monastery too, was disturbed, and changed to land of blood (Akeladam) in August 1998, the insiders are talking about it.
What astounded most was not the aggravation of revengeful enmity between the two sides, but the fact that the church officials didn't want to take any take any decisions..
This problem the religious problem which that is now considered as simple is feared that it may turn out to be difficult, he said.
If those regarded heretic are really found to be so, first like the fore-fathers a congregation would be called and there if they do not confess their sins and return, church would officially declare their sanctions otherwise concerned orthodox bodies say that if church becomes negligent of all these and let people to be sent in exile, applying the principle of "thorn by the thorn" would make it unable to withstand the enemy force within..
This dangerous situation within the Orthodox Church which hasn't been settled for more than half a year now, but is just waiting time to catch fire has saddened those who have true orthodox love.
The religious organization who want these eloquent people with wide knowledge of the church but were violently shoved by church leaders are man, and hence, authorities in the Orthodox Church should have given urgent resolve for such kind of religious controversies..
But as if Orthodox Church is without owner, it's regrettable to see no one whose sympathizer whenever a problem arises.           .
The clergy who controls the two sides hasn't said anything against the so-called heretic or the accusers.
Nor is there any officials statement that comes out of her, she's still soun asleep..
The fight between each other has surpassed the country and continued overseas..
Therefore, Aba Ketsela Mengistu, who lives abroad condemned his defamation from where believes..
This discord between the two orthodox followers unless it gets remedy from now, it is not difficult to predict that the process is going to bring about harm to the church.  .
From Fiameta September 25, 1998
To Make His Love Steady with the Catholics.
The patriarch's Journey to Romania Brought Criticism!
Years have elapsed since he was greeted with storms of oppositions as well as criticisms.
However, the patriarch staggeringly clings to his authority, despite all these criticism and sarcasm, for he has become used to them.
The oppositions as they are, the patriarch's journey to Romania last week has been a corridor talk among the clergy.
Among the criticisms suggested with regards to his journey is the fact that no other religious leader goes to such an annual assembly sponsored by Catholic Church, except being represented; although various religious groups are invited apart from Christians, in this annual conference which is said to be organized for world peace, it was embarrassing for Ethiopian Orthodox church to be represented by its patriarch while others sent their representatives, the report stated.
The clergy who said "To make his love steady with the Catholics", also criticized the message he relayed as he went overseas, and termed it "lacking truth and unexpected form a holy father".
He lied when he said he was called by Romanian Patriarch and President and tried to camouflage the truth, for the annual assembly that has so far been represented only by high priests. .
Sources who knew about this annual preaching and prayer session which is sponsored by Catholic Church, in the name of world peace, and held at different places every year, more than 30 denominations and other religions like Islam would be represented but not by their leaders
These are not the only criticisms showered on the patriarch.
Rather than nominally and symbolically sitting with Ato Simon Mechale and count aid money for the current national problem, some say it would have been much fruitful if he went overseas and collect aid for our follow victims..
Although some who saw him on the national TV receiving aid wondered why he doesn't rather go overseas to collect aid, those who knew the secret that made him lose heart repeatedly stated that he won't ever take his leg abroad, where Ethiopians live, for he doesn't want anymore damaged eggs to be thrown at him.
He was confident with his recent trip to Romania he was fully cognizant of the fact that these aren't as many Ethiopians there..
It has been heard that patriarch was quoted as saying that "the war and famine that befell upon the Tigrean People just after they opposed him", is the rage of his sadness and prayer.
As close sources disclose, many personnel in the clergy were very saddened with this remark, and infact, in one tabloid, he was quoted as saying "on the morrow of their opposition against me, they were bombed..
Because Tigrean people are sensitive to their religion, respectful of their history, and have steadfast faith, it would consider the patriarch's outpouring far from trust and embarrassing..
Aba Paulos, who went to Romania together with his personal, friend Aba Germia, with the church money, would have gone to Tigray during this turbulent time and with an apology could have showed solidarity and expressed sympathy, however, it seems out of revenge, that he hasn't stepped on the soil of Tigray for so many months how, told those groups who felt the suffering of Tigray..
From Fiameta, September 6, 1998
Ethiopia Didn't Receive Egyptian Aid!
The Egyptian Ambassador said, "We don't know the reason"
Various comments were for warded in relation to Egyptian government's material aid to Eritrea..
With regards to this, we asked Egyptian Ambassador to Ethiopia, Marwan Bedir, in an interview he gave us in Embassy..
Thanking him for his cooperation, we presented here part of the interview..
Fiameta: Mr. Ambassador, recently you gave aid to Eritrean government..
But when you wanted to give similar aid to Ethiopia, it was reported that you were given no response..
Which body said we won't receive this aid? What was the reason.
Ambassador Marwan Bedir we don't know why they said they won't receive the aid; as to the body who refreshed the offer, we disclosed in our press statement.
Fiameta Anyway, how was the aid to be conducted?
Ambassador: On our side, we have an interest to cooperatively work with other African countries..
We have 320 experts working in different African countries.  Among these more than half are doctors..
Our request to offer the help and cooperation the kind of doctors Ethiopia need didn't get response..
Last time at the bomb blast in Nairobi we offered similar help..
Our minister of health himself went to Nairobi..
The minister is a surgeon..
For people who need plastic surgery, he took them with his people to Cairo and did the surgery himself..
We cooperate in all sectors with other African countries..
But Ethiopia wasn't willing..
For those who give us positive response, we do the necessary cooperation..
Unless it's exaggerated due to the clash Eritrea has with Ethiopia, what's wrong with one county helping another? For example, Italy and Germany helped millions of dollars to Eritrea and they are still helping..
Nobody mentions this European aid..
We don't know why the Egyptian part is magnified..
Wh doesn't appropriate news apply to Egypt?.
It's very disappointing..
As yet, with our relations to Ethiopia, it's the Addis Ababa University and colleges that give us positive responses..
For the medical aid we provide now, the ministry of foreign affairs and Ministry of Health haven't provided us response..
Fiameta: Instead of putting your request through the ministry of foreign affairs, why don't you directly give for the Relief and Rehabilitation commission who's responsible for this?
Ambassador: Our relation is with ministry of foreign affairs..
We don't want to make things complicated again..
According to our common working practice, our situation and quest should be responded by ministry of foreign affairs..
We have up to now good relations..
The problem is we didn't get quick response..
On our side, we would continue the help we provide for Ethiopia, he responded..
From Fiameta August 30, 1998
Ethio-Eritrean Boarder Demarcation Begins from the East
Ethiopian and Eritrean border demarcation begins from the past, United Nations news source, IRIN, disclosed.
IRIN quoting the discussion held between the two higher bodies in London last week, pointed out that the disclosure of the border demarcation that was said to start from the east was made during the London meeting the independent Ethio-Eritrean border demarcation commission prepared.
IRIN quoting close diplomatic sources to the process also reported the fact that the border demarcation that covers one thousand kilometers begins in the east is within the liking of Ethiopia.
In the London meeting United Nation Mission for Ethio-Eritrea (UNMEE) head and representative of the general secretary, Kofi Anan, Legwala Joseph was present..
In the Ethio-Eritrean of border demarcation that was made official in April last year, it was to be recalled that additional clear explanation was asked on the different areas of western sides including Bademe.
The Ethio-Eritrea border demarcation would be carried out in the coming May, it was to be recalled.
From Addis Zemen February 20, 2003
Artist Jiji Presented a Special concert in Athens to Express Appreciation to Athlete.
A special Music Festival that enabled the gathering of many Ethiopians was conducted in Athens which is hosting the 28th Olympiad competition.
Reuters reported yesterday that in a music festival that was conducted on Saturday night the star artist was the popular singer Ejigayehu Shibabaw (Jiji).
Jiji who appeared in a white traditional dress and beautified with golden jewelries spend the night praising the former and the current Olympic winners.
In music festival conducted at Galazio Night Club in Athens, Major Haile Gebre Selassie as well as athelete Kenenisa Bekele and Sileshi Sehen who astonished the world in the ten thousand metes competition were present.  .
"The special program that took place at Kipseli," and in an area where most Ethiopians live, not less than 300 people were gathered.
In the Saturday's victory-news night, the audience couldn't help but dance standing from their seats being immersed with Jiji, who is born for an art and with her majestic movements and grandiloquent voice.
This music festival night, in which the Saturday's victory-news of the athletes was reflected, left an unforgettable memory for Ethiopians.
It also was a night that witnessed music and sports have international characteristics.  .
It was disclosed that athlete Kenenisa, followed by his country fellow athlete Sileshi, completed the Athens ten thousand meters in 27 minutes 05.10 second, registering a new record..
From Addis Zemen August 27, 2004
New Historical relics were found at around the place where obelisk of Axum Stoo.
The United Nations Education, Science and cultural organization (UNESCO) disclosed that it has discovered new historical sites at around the place where the obelisk of Axum and at other Axum sites where international relics were registered.
In the statement UNESCO disclosed yesterday, the new historical relies were discovered last week by he team of experts which was sent by UNESCO to help fix the obelisk of Axum.
According to Elizzbeth Wangari an expert of UNESCO's Centre for Relics, and Jum William, member of the organization's International Historical Relics, the newly found relics which were discovered at a location the obelisk of Axum previously stood, were different rooms and graves of emperors.
In the area of these new discoveries, there are several graves of emperor, it was proved through the study made by various experts of the team, the statement disclosed.
When Kochiro Matu Sura UNESCO's Director heard the news of the new discovery, he said that the fact that the discovered relics are grave yards become "a great and useful discovery", expressing his admiration.
The phenomenon that was brought about by the trial not only invites researchers to work more, it would make Axum an international centre for relics research, the statement of UNESCO pointed out, and this in turn, would have great contribution to Ethiopian Tourism economic development, it stated.
Foldofo Fatovich, leader of the geological research higher experts' team expressed that especially the graveyard discoveries would be studied deeply at a laboratory institution in one university in Italy.
The following graveyard researches would be done with Italian and Ethiopian governments full recognition and permission, UNSCO disclosed.        .
The expert team that came to Ethiopia to help fix the obelisk of Axum possesses modern hi-tech instruments that look in to the earth's situation easily, including the radar of the earth, and collect information, it was pointed out.
From Addis Zemen April 27, 2005
More than Three Hundred International Observers are Said to be Engaged.
In the May election more than three hundred international observers are said to be engaged, the chairman of the Ethiopian National Electoral Board disclosed.
Mr. Kemal Bedri, the chairman, in the statement he gave to local and international journalists yesterday disclosed that international observers are represented from African Union, European Union, Arab League and Carter Center as well as from embassies of different countries.
Among the ones who asked to observe the election and that have diplomatic missions, American, Japan, China, India and Turkey embassies, the chairman pointed out. .
In this year's election, 319 international observers got permissions up to now; Japan and China embassies have interest to engage additional observers other than the ones whom they assigned earlier, he disclosed.
Regarding local observers, those who have assuredly got permission as yet are three religious organizations, he pointed out..
On the other hand, the board reminded that any decision related to the election process that political parties give in the electoral offices should respect the ethics of election activities which the board releases accordingly..
No candidate could place its poster and its symbol of candidacy out of the regions it competes.
Within a 500 diameter of a polling station it is forbidden to carry out political agitation, the instruction the board released pointed out. .

Although Daniel Comen didn't compete in this race four other Kenyans challenged Haile.
Out of these Kenyans, Paul Coch and Tom Niyark come out second and third.

And this doesn't worry me.
I am still a growing youth.
I have much time to break additional records."
He said.
In this Greenpree race Haile was snatched his 10,000 meters record.

The victories of Kenyans were not only these.
Apart from registering second place in 5,000 and 10,000 meters by Thomas Itark and Paul Kochi, respectively, the Kenyans have become record holders in men's 800 and 3,000 meters.

He stood victorious in this race finishing in 7 minutes 26.2 second.
The Ethiopian jewel and who, at this time is given a name "one for its mother", have given an interview to Tobia newspaper with regards to the snatching of records, which he said "I am in a struggle.

And as he said, he's in a struggle.

From Tobia November 13, 1997
Ethiopian Telecommunication Corporation Disclosed that it's Property that Costs 5 Million Birr was Destroyed.
Due to the blaze and plundering on its west Addis Ababa office on April 18, 2001, Ethiopian Telecommunication Corporation be fell around 50 million Birr loss and couldn't give service for its 23 thousand clients.
In a communiqué it issued yesterday, 43 thousand lines digital stations, 10 line analog station, power giving bill information, files, computers and various tools as well as 10 vehicles, building parts an office materials some all in all, and others partially burned, resulting in up to 50 million Birr loss, Solomon Getachew reported quoting the communiqué.
What has been understood from the communiqué is that 23 thousand customers have fully lost service.
6 thousand customers at Kolfe and Shegole area couldn't make external calls, apart form the internal calls.
The corporation expressed that it needs a lot of work force, money and long time so as to do well again, and this would lag the efforts it started to reach the different parts of the country giving its services, the communiqué disclosed.
Finally, it would do its level best to restart the services that has been disrupted and cognizant of this, it reminded its customers to wait patiently..

From Fiameta August 30, 1998
The Bidding Farewell of Producers of Fiameta Newspape.
We feel sad to fall short while it's possible to work numerous things.
The producers and editors of Fiameta newspaper, Dawit Kebede and Biruk Kebede, are among the modern Ethiopians who have greatly contributed to the free press.
They worked a lot, made a lot of efforts...but their fruits of labor became suffering in TPLF/EPRDF prisons.
What the editors time and again are saying is "Let's save the next generation sacrificing our lives today..
And this is something expected from a truthful and strong Ethiopian and, hence, this is a saying that makes one proud.
However, nobody wants them to be the only one who should take the sacrifice, and we who work with them at Fiameta news papers wanted to share their pain...so we decided to be with them.
Especially, on the publisher and Editor-in-chief, Mr. Dawit Kebede, measures have been taken starting from being kidnapped by special bodies that TPLF/EPRDF trained up to being imprisoned in an underground cell.
At the moment, more than twelve charges have been filed against him and he's being disputing his case and paid in hundred thousands for bail.
Nevertheless, the decision the judges passed even now on him to stay behind bars at the central police is a witness as to what the final verdict could be on the editor.
The editor of the newspapers Dawit Bekele didn't want to discontinue his job and career even while he's in the midst to this difficult testing period.
Although working with devotion and with clear purpose is basic characteristic of Ethiopians in general, we don't want him to pay unnecessary sacrifice.
That's why we decided that the two siblings, Dawit Kebede and Biruk Kebede, be temporarily withdrawn from this career and we want the friends of Fiameta, in the county and overseas to realize this.
We want to use this opportunity to disclose that our producer and editior-in-chier is a life-long member of the International Press Institute, member of media and Information in the United Nations, ECA, and the executive member and public relations Officer of the Free Press Journalist Association.

From Tobia September 25, 1997
Ethiopian National Bank Announced that it has printed the new Birr note..
550 stations would give service of Birr note exchange
Solomon Teumelesa.
The Ethiopian National Bank disclosed that it has printed a new Birr note that would put in to use in the future and it has made enough preparation to start the work..
The governor of the bank Mr. Dubale Jale in his press statement yesterday disclosed that the printing of the new Birr note was distributed to the selected major areas in order to start exchange service..
He also made if official that the prepared money were 1, 5, 10, 50 and 100 Birr notes.
He also reminded that the old Birr notes has to be exchanged within 50 days form the day the money exchange is to be announced in the media sometime in the future..
He also explained that 21 days were allotted for the exchange of 50 and 100 Birr while 50 days were given for 1, 5 and 10 Birr notes..
The reason why various days were allotted to the Birr notes is that the 50 and 100 Birr notes are believed mostly to be found around cities, so these notes could be exchanged swiftly..
Mr.Dubale told that since the 1, 5 and 10 Birr notes are widely used by the country people, and they may find media difficulties, additional days were allotted..
Mr.Dubale pointed out that in order to make the exchange of Birr notes, 20 major stations were set up that coordinate branch office banks and temporary stations, and these stations are found in Addis Ababa, mekele, Dessie, Woldia, Gondar, Bahir Dar, Debre Markos, Debreberhan, Nazareth, Awassa, Shahemene, Asela, wolayta, Sodo, Hageremariam, Nekemte, Gimbi, Meth, Jima, Diredawa and Harar cities..
In addition where there are no brances of banks, three hundred temporary stations that give money exchange services are set up, Mr. Doubale explained..
250 government and private banks give the exchange services and in general 550 exchange stations are to be established, it was disclosed..
In order to do his work, two thousand workers were assigned and enough work instructions are setup, the necessary materials and tools for the exchange of Birr have already been prepared, he explained..
Both new and old Birr notes would be functional side by side starting form the date the bank officially discloses the exchange of the money until the last date, so till that last day, it would be illegal to disqualify the old Birr note, he underscored..
In order to avoid such and related problems, preparations have been underway to give appropriate awareness for the community, Mr. Dubale explained.
Different posters have been prepared to make people aware of the new Birr notes, it's reported.
The public created enough cooperation with regional police and armies of the defense force in order to protect trouble some and those who are engaged in looting activities.
Since the new Birr notes are made cautiously, it would be difficult to forge replication, said Mr. Dubale, And added that they are made in such a way that the public could identify and put in to use. .
Related to this he pointed out that the cents that are in use at the moment won't be changed..
It is to be recalled that the Birr notes which are in use at present were produced some 20 years ago.

Have They Missed it Now or Were They not Having It Even Before.

What is saddening, however, is the diffusion of hatred among people under the cover of this beautiful idea; in the confusion, rather than the people, as was propagated, the beneficiaries are few.

We say.

Because the result of defending racist stand with racism, the politics of arrogance with another arrogant and provocative politics would be destruction;

From Addis Zemen June 2, 2001
His Majesty's Funeral Has Become Controversial!
An Ascetic terrorizes claiming that if the corpse of Emperor Haileselassie I doesn't rest in honor, Ethiopia won't be peaceful!!
After being killed on August 29, 1974, the corps was found in a well that was dug next to the toilet of Mengistu Hailemariam, has not been officially buried with absolution and funeral ceremony, which has become the main topic of discussion recently.
After the corpse was found through digging, it is to be recalled that as to whether it was really his, his ex-personal doctor, professor Asrat Woldeyes certified.
After a year EPFDF came to power during the transition government individuals from the clergy, patriots' Association, and families were chosen and allowed to get in to the palace to find His majesty's corpse were given responsibilities and authority from investigating various documents up to having dug the places where he was said to be buried, and finally got the corpse.
In order to carry out the funeral ceremony after the corpse was found, the Ethiopian Patriots Association and the then MOA Anbessa Organization entered in to dispute that led the delay of the funeral.
Again after the dispute was made to calm down and at the time the preparation for the funeral ceremony was about to be carried out, people's revolt came about.
The question was "His majesty's funeral should not be carried out just like any ordinary individual".
The other question the opposition raised seven years before was "Let government declare a one-day mourning and carry out the funeral ceremony..."
His majesty was not only a father of Ethiopia but also for Africa, so government would give focus and he would be buried with the participation of the public.
Since there were ideas like these, the issue was asked to pass or to the people instead of just the MOA Anbessa and the Patriots' Association.
Based on this, with a seal of Patriots' Association and the signature of the chairman this question was put forward to the transitional government but couldn't get urgent response.
The preparation for the funeral ceremony was made to discontinue and based on the consent of the crown-prince in England and the people the funeral ceremony was decided to be carried out at another time.
The elderly people that were chosen to negotiate MOA Anbessa and the patriots' associations then formed a committee and started their activities, but they were not able to continue up to the end.
However, since 1995, ascetics who claimed to have seen a vision came to Addis Ababa told, "If His majesty's corpse don not rest in honor, a very great turmoil would be created" and terrorized the families of the king as well as the public, the committee that constituted elders started again its activities to carry out the ceremony in 1995.
Nevertheless, since this elderly committee who were formed to carry out the funeral ceremony needed to be legal body it has continued its effort to be a legal body and to be given full authority to carry out the funeral ceremony from 1995-1999 and it's to recalled that last years it got a government permission...The Haileselase I Memorial Organization.
Since the organization got this permission, it has met various obstacles to carry out the funeral ceremony.
Issues starting from whether to make the funeral ceremony on a holiday, to calling popular personality's form abroad to Ethiopia have become contentious.
Actually the situation was just like what the ascetic said that the country seemed to stay in drought and war until his majesty's corpse came to rest in honor.
As Fiameta newspapers was following the matter closely it falls upon it a responsibility to present to the public the ongoing disputes with regards to the funeral ceremony.
Among the disputes raised recently is found that there was a dispatch on the internet and in some tabloids that claimed the king's family living abroad didn't accept the legal body formed by the name Haileselassie I Memorial Organization and the fact that the funeral ceremony was to be carried out together with TPLF individuals, which saddened the organization.
In the statement the organization released last week, disclosed that the king's family didn't say that and the news was far from truth.
Some sources said that it's Lord Mengesha's line of the king family who exaggerate this.
There are still others who claim that this was just defamation of an ordinary nature.
Anyway, the controversy continued.
The other which seems ordinary, but whenever the funeral ceremony is mentioned creates a dispute is how the corpse is transported how the procession make its way.
They all seem to agree on one point.
The corpse would be taken out from the St. Mary church where it had been put temporarily and move by St. Gabriel church making its was by ministry of Foreign Affairs and passing by the Jubilee Palace, the corpse heads to Masquel Square where it rests for a while.
At masquel Square in the presence of invited guests and the public a ceremony of delivery speech for the occasion would be carried out.
It's the procession after this that became disputable.
One of the sides say that after the masquel square, the corpse would go to Laghar then through Churchil Road make its way to St. George church; then by piazza to Arat Kilo, Holy Trinity Cathedral, while the other group from Masquel Square, through Laghar straight to Mexico Avenue and would make its way to Tekle Haimanot Church, Passing the General Habte Ghiorgis bridge would reach to St. George church, then via Afincho Ber by the side of the University take rest at miskiyazunal church.
This seemingly ordinary, but disputable issue has not been resolved as yet.
However, there's a point which all agree.
The reason they have for the corpse to come at Miskiyazunal church which is found next to Teferi Makonnen School, was that "the miskiyazunal Ark of the Tabernacle was in exile together with the king His majesty, and came back afterwards and a church was built to it, and up to 1974 it was administered from his majesty' personal savings".
Therefore, it's after the corpse reposed here that it should go down wards to Holy Trinity Cathedral, they say.
The other and the main contentious issue was as to when the funeral ceremony would be carried out? This is the question.
According to the internal sources, the funeral ceremony was planned to be carried on the coming may 5, 2000 for its Freedom Day and there won't be any work.
But since this would be most regrettable and shameful act, it's already been criticized.
May 5 is Independent day.
It was a holy the day the Italians went out fully from Ethiopia and it was a day when His majesty came back to Addis Ababa.
To bury His majesty on such a great independent day would not only be sorrowful, it would also be interpreted differently among others.
Changing Independent day by a Funeral day is like committing crime on a generation.
Therefore, by any standard, making may 5 a funeral day would be an unforgivable mistake.
The Haileselassie I memorial organization is by now preparing a letter to the prime Minster in order to carry out the funeral ceremony on this date.
The other problem of May 5 is that the time where EPRDF and other oppositions would make fierce struggle for the upcoming election.
In addition, there's a worry that time government and private Medias would be focusing on the election and the funeral ceremony could be underestimated.
Apart from this, dates chosen for the funeral ceremony are July 24, His majesty's birthday, August 29 the date on which he was killed by the Derge regime, October 31 his day of coronation, all of which were unaccepted for one reason or another.
And so the dispute continues.
But the people have some decisive questions.
Why does the HaileSelasse I organization need to carryout the funeral ceremony along with other holidays?  Why can't the funeral ceremony be held on a separate day?  Why couldn't it be on any ordinary Saturday and Sunday when people are free?  These are the questions raised.

The Second Segment of the Axum Obelisk Arrived

The member of the committee of or the Return of the Axum Obelisk, Mr. Fisseha Zebelo disclosed that the part which reached Axum town yesterday is the base of the obelisk.

The Italian Ambassador for Ethiopia, Guido Latela, expressed on the occasion said that the fact that Axum obelisk returned home after 68 years in Rome would enable to grow the economic and social cooperation apart form strengthening the relationship of the two counties.
The third segment and the top most part of the obelisk is scheduled to arrive have next Monday, the ambassador disclosed.

When the first segment of the obelisk arrived in Axum last Tuesday more than 50 thousand residents, higher government officials and guests were present.

A Russian scientist has told a Moscow City court that the information an American businessman allegedly tried to purchase about a Russian torpedo is commonly available and not a state secret.

In 1998, the United States voted against the creation of the World's first permanent International War Crimes Court.
President Clinton still has a chance to sign the treaty creating the Court before a final deadline this Sunday.
Advocates are pressing him to do just that, but Conservatives in Congress and Pentagon officials don't want the US to join the treaty.
The World's Jeb Sharp explains why.
Jesse Helms, the Conservative and powerful Chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, has made it clear the Rome's statuette would be dead on arrival if it were brought to Congress for ratification.
But proponents of the permanent International Criminal Court would still like to see President Clinton at least sign the treaty before the New Year's eve deadline.
Richard Dicker of Human Rights Watch says Clinton's signature would be an important symbolic gesture.
What he will accomplish is making a clear statement that the United States not only in the former Yugoslavia, not only in Rwanda, not only in Cambodia, not only in Sierra Leone, where the administration has supported efforts at justice, but worldwide the United States supports the rule of law and supports holding those accused of genocide to account under the highest standards of due process.
But the opposition here in the United States is intense.
It comes mainly from the Pentagon where US military officials fear the Court will leave Americans vulnerable to politically motivated prosecutions.
Negotiators have tried to include safeguards in the treaty to address those fears, but stop short of exempting US personnel from prosecution.
John Bolton of the American Enterprise Institute shares the Pentagon's objections.
I think there is every prospect such a court and its prosecutor would be highly politicized and the principal target of a court like this might well turn out to be the United States or Israel or other countries like that.
Bolton says that almost happened at the War Crimes Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in The Hague, when Chief Prosecutor Carla Delponte briefly contemplated an investigation of NATO's bombing campaign against Serbia in 1999.
But proponents of the court say it's healthy for the United States and its allies to come under the same scrutiny as other countries.
Richard Dicker of Human Rights Watch says Delponte's handling of the NATO case was exemplary.
Carla Delponte was acting as any responsible prosecutor must when she receives credible allegations of wrongdoing.
She looked into those allegations and then after an appropriate investigation she dismissed them.
Richard Dicker says President Clinton should keep the promise he made to the Rwandan people in 1998 when he told survivors of the genocide there the United States would support the International Court.
But John Bolton of the American Enterprise Institute says a Clinton signature in the face of stiff domestic opposition would be meaningless.
I think it's a symbolic act that doesn't achieve much, but I don't think anybody internationally should think that whatever President Clinton does will have the slightest impact on the next administration.
Despite American objections, the International Criminal Court enjoys wide support worldwide and among major US allies.
131 countries have signed the treaty, 7 today and 25 have ratified it.
60 nations in all must ratify the treaty for the International Criminal Court to come into existence.
That's expected to happen, with or without US support, in 2002.
For The World, I'm Jeb Sharp.
This is PRI, Public Radio International.

The airdrop -- one of the biggest paratroop drops in decades -- was a dramatic entry for ground troops into a region where only small groups of U.S. special forces have been operating.
Coalition airstrikes have been hitting Iraqi military forces and other strategic targets in the north.
This tightens the noose against Saddam's forces battling coalition forces to the south,'' Brig. Gen. James Parker, commander of U.S. forces in the north.
And it may also serve as a warning to Turkish forces.''
Giving cover for the deployment, U.S. warplanes struck Iraqi ground troops and bunkers in northern Iraq.
Three waves of combat planes from the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt hit ``ground troops, command and control bunkers, artillery positions and ... a surface to air missile battery,'' said Lt. John Oliveira, the ship's public affair officer.
Around dawn Thursday, strikes resumed, with a massive explosion just outside the Kurdish zone close to the village of Kalak.
Warplanes pounded forward Iraqi positions in the hills overlooking Chamchamal, 35 kilometers (22 miles) east of the key oil city of Kirkuk.
Later Thursday, Kurdish troops in Chamchamal advanced their positions between government-controlled and rebel-controlled areas, taking over a Iraqi check point on their front with no fighting at this point, witnesses said.
Early Thursday, Kurdish fighters closed off a highway and roads near the airstrip where troops were said to be arriving, outside the town of Bashur, about 30 miles (50 kilometers) northeast of the Kurd-controlled city of Irbil and 30 miles (50 kilometers) south of the Turkish border.
From the highway, dusted from a recent snow, a flashing light from the airstrip's control tower was visible in the distance, and three helicopters could be seen landing, flying with nearly all their lights extinguished.
Future airlifts into the area will include supplies and support personnel for the 173rd's fighters, defense officials said.
The airfield's 6,700-foot (2,042-meter) runway is long enough to land C-17s and other U.S. military cargo planes.
Lt. Col. Thomas Collins, a spokesman for the U.S. Army's Southern European Task Force, refused to say whether the paratroopers deployed directly from Italy into Iraq or had taken a different route.
The matter immediately sparked controversy in Italy, where there is a strong anti-war movement.
The country's parliament voted this month to allow U.S.-led coalition forces to use Italian air space and military bases -- but not for directs attacks on Iraq.
Pentagon officials have said for weeks they would have U.S. forces in northern Iraq to open another front against Saddam's forces.
The vast majority of the coalition ground troops in Iraq are moving toward Baghdad from the south after entering from Kuwait.
Pentagon officials had hoped to have the Army's 4th Infantry Division invade Iraq from the north, but Turkey balked at allowing up to 62,000 U.S. troops on its soil to prepare for that option.
The use of the 173rd shows the military has shifted to a smaller, lighter force.
Military officials say they would have liked to have secured key oil fields around the northern cities of Mosul and Kirkuk -- and perhaps the cities themselves -- by now.
Though no hostilities were expected during the deployment, the 173rd decided to parachute in rather then ferry troops in by plane so that a significant combat force could mass almost immediately to protect itself, officers said, according to a U.S. reporter traveling with the 173rd.
Kirkuk is key.
The Iraqi's want it, the Kurds want it, the Turks want it and various other ethnic groups also want it,'' Maj. Mike Hastings said.
What this drop means is that we can secure it until we are relieved by other forces.''
Besides Mosul and Kirkuk, another key target in northern Iraq is Tikrit, Saddam's hometown and the tribal center for most of his inner circle.
Most of the Adnan Division of the Republican Guard relocated from the Mosul area to the Tikrit area shortly before the war began.
Another key mission for the 173rd could be to keep order in northern Iraq, which is controlled by two semi-autonomous Kurdish factions but also includes several splinter groups and a base for the al-Qaida-linked Ansar al-Islam.
Turkey has said it may send more troops into northern Iraq to prevent refugees from moving north, while U.S. officials have said they advised Turkey against sending large additional forces into northern Iraq.

A U.S.-sponsored forum that brought Iraqi opposition leaders together to shape the country's postwar government began Tuesday with a U.S. promise not to rule Iraq and concluded with an agreement to meet again in 10 days.
Meeting in the biblical birthplace of the prophet Abraham, delegates from Iraq's many factions discussed the role of religion in the future government and ways to rebuild the country.
But some Shiite Muslim groups boycotted the meeting and thousands protested nearby.
A 13-point statement released after the meeting stressed the need to work toward a democratic Iraq built on the rule of law and equality.
It also called for dissolving Saddam's Baath Party but left open the question of separating church from the state.
Retired Lt. Gen. Jay Garner, who will head the U.S.-led interim administration in Iraq, opened the conference under a golden-colored tent in the shadows of the 4,000-year-old ziggurat at Ur, a terraced temple platform of the ancient Sumerians.
What better birthday can a man have than to begin it not only where civilization began but where a free Iraq and a democratic Iraq will begin today?'' said Garner, who turned 65 Tuesday and wore a twin American and Iraqi flag pin on his blue shirt.
White House envoy Zalmay Khalilzad told delegates that the United States has ``no interest, absolutely no interest, in ruling Iraq.''
We want you to establish your own democratic system based on Iraqi traditions and values,'' Khalilzad said.
I urge you to take this opportunity to cooperate with each other.''
Participants included Kurds, Sunnis and Shiites from inside the country and others who spent years in exile.
U.S. officials invited the groups, which picked their own representatives.
Many Iraqis boycotted the meeting in opposition to U.S. plans to install Garner atop an interim administration.
Thousands of Shiites -- who constitute Iraq's most populous religious group but were repressed under Saddam Hussein -- demonstrated in nearby Nasiriyah, chanting ``No to America and no to Saddam!''
Iraq needs an Iraqi interim government.
Anything other than this tramples the rights of the Iraqi people and will be a return to the era of colonization,'' said Abdul Aziz Hakim, a leader of the largest Iraqi Shiite group, the Supreme Council for Islamic Revolution in Iraq.
U.S. officials hope more Iraqis join the process and stressed that this was just the first of many such meetings in Iraq.
The meeting concluded with the delegates voting by show of hands to meet again in 10 days.
A national conference is planned to select the interim administration, perhaps within weeks, a senior U.S. official said on condition of anonymity.
The interim administration could begin handing power back to Iraqi officials within three to six months, but forming a government will take longer, said Maj. Gen. Tim Cross, the top British member of Garner's team.
One has to go through the process of building from the bottom up, allowing the leadership to establish itself, and then the election process to go through and so forth,'' Cross said.
That full electoral process may well take longer.''
Garner's Office of Reconstruction and Humanitarian Assistance is charged with coordinating humanitarian assistance, rebuilding infrastructure shattered by years of war and U.N. sanctions, and gradually handing back power to Iraqis leading a democratically elected government.
Tuesday's meeting was the first step toward that goal after the ouster of Saddam.

British Prime Minister Tony Blair arrives in Russia today for talks with Vladimir Putin on security, foreign policy, and economic issues.
They are also expected to discuss a new Russian proposal for deep cuts in US and Russian long-range missiles.
VOA's Larry James in Moscow.
The highlight of the one-day visit will be three hours of talks on Tuesday, during which Mr. Blair and Mr. Putin will focus on a wide range of issues including Russia's latest call for cutting the number of strategic nuclear warheads to below 1500.
President Clinton has said such a deal is possible, but that it will be first necessary to convince Moscow of the merits of America's proposed Missile Defense System.
The US wants to amend the 1972 Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty so it can develop such a system.
Russia believes such a move could spark a new arms race and has threatened to tear up existing weapons agreements and stop disarmament talks if the United States goes ahead.
On Sunday Mr. Putin called on the Russian parliament to quickly ratify the amended Conventional Forces in Europe Treaty.
That treaty requires Russia to make further non-nuclear weapons reductions in some areas of the country including breakaway Chechnya.
President Putin acknowledged that Russia is still violating its commitment in Chechnya, but he said it is only a temporary situation which has the ultimate aim of cutting armaments in the region.
He also thanked the 29 other signatories to the treaty for their understanding.
He said Russia is fully behind the agreement that, he said, is an efficient instrument of ensuring security in Europe for years to come.
The original treaty was signed in 1990 and led to the destruction of thousands of heavy weapons by NATO and the former Warsaw Pact.
Tony Blair became the first western leader to come to Russia to meet the new President last March even before Mr. Putin was elected.
The Russian leader returned the favor by making London one of his first foreign destinations after taking office.
The two have already met four times this year.
Analysts here in Moscow believe Britain can play a useful role as a bridge to both Europe and the United States.
Trade is also expected to figure significantly in the talks.
Britain ranks as the third largest investor after the United States and Germany with just slightly more than $1 billion invested in Russia.
Larry James, VOA News, Moscow.

The war in Iraq could last months and require considerable US military reinforcements to assure a victory, the Washington Post reported Thursday, quoting senior US military officials.
Sandstorms, dangerously long supply lines and a recalcitrant enemy "has led to abroad reassessment by some top generals of US military expectations and timelines," the Post reports.
"Tell me how this ends," one senior officer asked the Post.
Most US army commanders believe it is critical to pause the breakneck advance towards Baghdad to secure the supply lines and make sure weapons are operable and troops resupplied after days of powerful sandstorms and damage inflicted by Iraqi attacks, the Post reports.
The Post also quoted Central Intelligence Agency and Pentagon intelligence analysts complaining that Bush officials largely ignored their warning that Iraqi irregular forces would use guerrilla tactics and offer significant resistance.
Publicly US officials have insisted that the war is going according to plan, and the most advanced US forces are currently some 100 kilometers (60 miles) outside of Baghdad.
